bearings.paper_claim: A learned query policy is needed only because the graph is unknown. OPT is greedy influence maximization on the full graph G* and is the ceiling; rewards are scaled as (influence minus CHANGE) over (OPT minus CHANGE), Eq. 1. With the graph known, greedy is the reference standard.
bearings.paper_location: Section 2 Problem description; Section 3.1 Eq. 1; Section 4 Performance metrics
bearings.system_side: budgetRecruit runs cost-bounded max-coverage greedy over the edge-probability matrix PE. Candidates are pruned to degree at least 0.1 x mean degree. The comment cites the 1-1/e guarantee and says no ML is needed at this scale.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper premise (learning pays only when edges are hidden) applies only if the cosponsor graph is a partial sample of a latent network. The 1-1/e guarantee holds for greedy on the graph as observed, not for the true network if ties are missing.
bearings.verifier_note: Reproduced: the code lines, the 1-1/e comment, the 0.1 x mean-degree pruning and the no-ML comment all match. Softened: the analyst says OPT is greedy on the observed graph. In the paper OPT is greedy on the full graph (the ceiling), and the policy's oracle O is greedy on the discovered graph. Corrected in paper_claim above.

bearings.paper_claim: Geometric-DQN, trained per family and tested on held-out networks of that family, improves influence by 7.91 to 26.6 percent of the CHANGE-to-OPT gap (best variant per family, 13 test networks, IC p = 0.1, budget 10, T = 5 queries). Discovered graphs are almost always larger than CHANGE's, yet size does not correlate with influence across Geometric-DQN policies.
bearings.paper_location: Section 4 Experiment setup; Section 5 Results, Table 4; Section 6 Insights, Size of the discovered graph
bearings.system_side: load_network reads the newest augmented congress_cosponsor_network workbook, falling back to a base file only when no AUG file exists (select_network_file, line 371). It then mean-symmetrizes the edges into a name-keyed adjacency dict. All listed edges are treated as observed, with no model of missing ties.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper discovery setting applies only if cosponsorship is an incomplete sample of a latent contact network. The paper numbers come from other networks under single-colour IC, so they cannot be carried over as system gains.
bearings.verifier_note: Reproduced: the 7.91 to 26.6 range and the per-family best-variant basis match Table 4. Softened: the code prefers the newest AUG file, not the newest complete one, and the word complete does not appear in the loader. The paper says almost always, not always. The claim that the component treats cosponsorship as the influence and alignment tie is not shown in the cited lines and is not verified.

bearings.paper_claim: Every comparison uses a single-colour independent cascade with uniform p = 0.1, budget 10, and the mean of 100 simulations, with no variance or confidence intervals. Tables 2 and 4 report the best Geometric-DQN variant per test network or per test set.
bearings.paper_location: Section 4 Experiment setup and performance metrics; Section 5 Results, Tables 2 and 4
bearings.system_side: The frontier runs a two-colour first-to-reach cascade over an edge-keyed splitmix common-random-number draw with default MC 20. Its kernel is p = x/(x+6), where x carries cpf_diffusion partisan damping and receiver susceptibility. Seeds come from lazy greedy over a priority queue on the fully known kernel P.

bearings.transfer_conditions: Gains measured under uniform p = 0.1 single-colour IC do not carry over to the system heterogeneous two-colour kernel. Any reuse needs a rerun on the system own P and stays UNVERIFIED until a second path reproduces it (DE-062).
bearings.verifier_note: Paper side reproduced from Section 4 and the Table captions. Code side reproduced: the edge-keyed CRN comment and draw, MC default 20, lazy greedy with a heap, p = x/(x+6), and two-colour cascade all match the cited lines. cpf_diffusion is described as dampening cross-party edges, consistent with the partisan wording.

bearings.paper_claim: A cheap query rule can prioritize which nodes to reveal under a fixed budget. H2 (minimum-degree node among those discovered in the last step) beats CHANGE on voles4 (72.8 vs 58.9), damascus (104.9 vs 95.2) and israel (34.2 vs 30.6), Table 5. The text says H2 picks nodes with higher true betweenness than CHANGE.
bearings.paper_location: Section 6 Insights, Table 5; Section 6 text on Figures 6 and 7 (figure values not extracted)
bearings.system_side: rank_outreach_candidates orders candidates by published PageRank (damping 0.85), then by origin plus target route cost. Its docstring says an incomplete search must not be read as evidence of no route. No budgeted acquisition policy for choosing which directories or people to resolve next appears in these lines.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Usable only as a data-collection priority, judged on graph-completeness metrics. Never judged on spread, access or introduction probability (D-025). Influence language stays barred on revolving-door edges. Any learned policy stays UNVERIFIED until a second path reproduces it (DE-062).
bearings.verifier_note: Reproduced: the Table 5 numbers quoted for voles4, damascus and israel match, and the betweenness claim matches the text. Softened: the cited lines say only that an incomplete route search is not evidence of no route. They do not say the staffer graph is assembled from partial directories and payroll, and they do not show that the code admits partial observation of the graph. The gap statement is not verified here.

related.why: Tambe group RL for contingency-aware IM, where invited seeds may refuse (uncertain seed take-up). Wilder is cited, not a co-author. Kamarthi handles an uncertain graph instead. The SGATE mapping is Paul's and was not checked here.
Chen, Wilder, Qiu, An, Rice and Tambe. Deep RL for influence maximization under complex contagion rather than IC. Checked against the author list and abstract.
Deep RL for influence maximization in closed networks by edge activation. Checked against the title and opening text. Kamarthi instead learns which nodes to query, so the match is method family only.

Graph embedding plus a GNN regressor for influence maximization. The embedding is struc2vec, not DeepWalk, and labels come from SIR and IC simulation, so the shared machinery is GNN-based embedding rather than DeepWalk and GCN.
Adaptive submodularity theory for sequential decisions under partial observability. It gives the guarantee-based alternative to Kamarthi learned query policy. Checked against the opening text.

Compares centrality heuristics with greedy and sampling methods on known networks. It is evidence on heuristic-versus-greedy, but not on the unknown-graph setting. The unknown-graph wording in the earlier link is removed.
Efficient greedy influence maximization under the independent cascade model, the same diffusion model Kamarthi uses as its oracle. Checked against the text on greedy and ICM.

summary_issues: Training scope is wrong. The summary says each policy is trained on 9 networks pooled across four families. The paper trains and tests per family (Section 4: train and deploy for each network family; Table 1). Each policy sees only its family's 2 or 3 training networks plus synthetic graphs, and is tested on that family's held-out networks.
The summary says the recruitment and frontier code states that no ML is needed. Only the recruitment template comment says this. budget_frontier.py has no such statement.

The summary calls the cosponsor graph a fully observed public record. That is the system's modelling assumption, as the code treats all listed edges as observed. It is not a verified fact about the data and should be labelled as an assumption.

The summary says H2 beats CHANGE on several test networks. That holds for voles3, voles4, damascus and israel. On the Homeless networks the gaps are small (b1 19.4 vs 19.1; spy2 16.4 vs 16.01), and H2 loses on rural3 (17.3 vs 17.4). The summary should not imply broad wins.
The 7.91 to 26.6 range and the 7-23 vs 7-26 inconsistency are reported correctly in the summary and need no change.
